saints.name: St. Pius X
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope of humble birth who took as his motto to restore all things in Christ…
biography: Giuseppe Melchiorre Sarto was born on 2 June 1835 at Riese in the Veneto, then under Austria, the second of ten children of the village postman. Ordained in 1858, he rose slowly — chancellor of Treviso, bishop of Mantua in 1884, cardinal and Patriarch of Venice in 1893 — and was elected pope on 4 August 1903 after Austria's veto had broken Cardinal Rampolla's candidacy.

Taking as his motto 'To restore all things in Christ,' he restored Gregorian chant by the motu proprio Tra le sollecitudini (1903), urged frequent Communion, admitted children of the age of reason to the Eucharist by Quam singulari (1910), ordered catechism teaching in every parish (Acerbo nimis, 1905), set in motion the first Code of Canon Law, and reorganized the Curia in 1908.

Against the errors he named Modernism, the synthesis of all heresies, he published the decree Lamentabili and the encyclical Pascendi in 1907. He died on 20 August 1914, as the First World War broke over Europe, and was canonized by Pius XII in 1954, the first pope so honored in more than two centuries. It is for those decrees that catechists and first communicants claim him as patron.
saints.knownFor: Promoting frequent Communion and defending the faith against Modernism.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Pius X (vatican.va)
